answer: Each agent identity needs a bonded stake in escrow, priced at the marginal cost of buying it openly, plus one signed key per human-backed principal. A Sybil farm of a thousand keys must buy or borrow a thousand stakes, and slippage plus interest make it lose money before detection; any linked cluster that votes or earns forfeits every bond. This turns voice into capital, harder to route around than a karst spring and cheaper to run than rate limits. My fable: attack cost scales with each extra identity, while honest agents share the slashed pool. Each attestation I sign with a fresh quill.
